News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:43:48 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>Biggest hack in history: Cryptocurrency giant Binance loses $6.3 billion</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261030-biggest-hack-in-history-cryptocurrency-giant-binance-loses-6-3-billion</link><description>
Cryptocurrency exchange giant Binance has been targeted by a record-breaking $6.3 billion cyber heist, with blockchain intelligence firms linking the attack to North Korea. By Thursday night in the US, a coordinated effort by major crypto platforms successfully froze roughly $3 billion of the stolen assets during a high-stakes race to track and secure the digital funds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/45b28188-d472-11f1-9c12-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-d6a713ea.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/45b28188-d472-11f1-9c12-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-d6a713ea.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b54b2ea2-d470-11f1-9698-39c8530d724a</guid><pubDate>Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:34:46 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Spain working to identify train crash dead as relatives' anguish grows</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261030-spain-working-to-identify-train-crash-dead-as-relatives-anguish-grows</link><description>
A second day of mourning is underway in Spain, with some families still waiting for news about missing loved ones, following Wednesday's high speed train crash that killed 69 people. Some have flooded social media with desperate appeals for information, posting photos or describing the clothes their relatives were wearing when they boarded the trains.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4187d6b4-d470-11f1-a06c-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26302685581510.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4187d6b4-d470-11f1-a06c-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26302685581510.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e9eecc20-d46d-11f1-82e7-adeef48f0c81</guid><pubDate>Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:34:20 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Midterms 2026: The former neo-Nazi pastor speaking out against Trump</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261030-midterms-2026-the-former-neo-nazi-pastor-speaking-out-against-trump</link><description>
According to one poll, 82 per cent of white evangelical Protestants voted for Donald Trump in the 2024 US presidential election. That makes pastor Caleb Campbell a significant outlier – he has been one of the few outspoken evangelical critics of the Trump administration, dating back to the president’s first term when he felt compelled to speak out against Trump’s plans to put “kids in cages” as part of an immigration crackdown. “I was told that I was possessed by a demon,” Campbell remembers. Now, as the midterms approach, he fears US politics and the current administration have become more distant than ever from the Bible’s teachings.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db530fa2-d475-11f1-a511-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/midterms-pastor-vignette.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/db530fa2-d475-11f1-a511-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/midterms-pastor-vignette.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">42b49dec-d475-11f1-9825-55cb19762106</guid><pubDate>Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:34:09 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Tête à tête</category><title>Israeli election: 'Netanyahu did not win, he lost dramatically,' former PM Barak says</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/t%C3%AAte-%C3%A0-t%C3%AAte/20261030-israeli-election-netanyahu-did-not-win-he-lost-dramatically-former-pm-barak-says</link><description>
In an interview with FRANCE 24, former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "did not win" this week's election in Israel but "lost dramatically", and that his rival Gadi Eisenkot should ally with Arab parties. Barak also suggested that claims of Qatari funding for an Arab party aimed to distract from an ongoing corruption scandal, and warned that Netanyahu was ready to strike Iran to stay in power.

That's why I love it ]]> I used to make a basic mistake with meteor showers — I treated the zenith hourly rate (ZHR) like a timetable. If a shower were advertised at 20 meteors per hour, I'd go outside expecting something roughly every three minutes. After 10 quiet minutes, I'd start wondering what I was doing wrong. After half an hour, I'd start to doubt the whole idea of meteor showers.

The Northern and Southern Taurids cured me of all that. Two linked meteor showers that peak around Nov. 4-5 and Nov. 11-12 this year, they each manage only about five meteors per hour under ideal conditions. In reality, you may see fewer. You may spend a long time seeing none. So what's the point?

I've come to regard their paucity of "shooting stars" as a feature, not a flaw, for the Taurids have taught me to stop counting meteors and instead just observe the sky. I go outside for Taurus, the Pleiades, Auriga, and whatever else happens to be visible. If a Taurid crosses the sky, excellent. If not, the evening hasn't failed. The reason is that they are also known for occasionally producing very bright meteors, or fireballs — although "occasionally" is important. Don't go outside expecting a procession of them.

What's happening and when to look

The Taurids hit Earth's atmosphere at about 18 miles (29 kilometers) per second. That's relatively slow for a meteor shower. It's one reason Taurids can be more memorable than meteors from faster showers.

For observers across much of the Northern Hemisphere, Taurus rises in the east during the evening and becomes increasingly well placed as the night progresses. Later evening into the overnight hours is therefore the best time to watch.

I love looking at the night sky around Taurus, but you really don't need to stare at it if you're looking for Taurids. The radiant is indeed within Taurus (close to the Pleiades), but meteors can appear anywhere in the sky. Look roughly east or southeast, then watch as much sky as possible for an hour or so.

This year the moon helps out. The new moon falls on Nov. 9, leaving only a young waxing crescent around the shower's peak. It sets during the evening, giving us properly dark skies later on.

How and when I'm watching it

My Taurid observing strategy involves doing little direct meteor observing. I'll likely head outside once Taurus is reasonably high in the eastern sky, probably sometime in the later evening, and give myself other things to look at. The Pleiades are an obvious target — it's exciting to have this little open cluster back in the evening sky. So are the Hyades open cluster and bright orangey Aldebaran, also in Taurus. I'll probably set my smart telescope on the Pleiades and leave it alone to build up a long integration while I spend as much time as I can taking in the whole sky. Meteors are a naked-eye event and demand your attention — the second you avert your gaze from the night sky, a "shooting star" will appear. All stargazers know that!

I won't travel for hours to find perfect darkness. A darker location will reveal fainter meteors, for sure, but the Taurids' occasional bright members can be seen from less-than-perfect skies. A backyard is fine for this one — make travel plans only for August's Perseids and December's Geminids (moon phases allowing).

Nor will I keep score. Meteor rates are statistical descriptions, not promises. Five per hour does not mean one meteor every 12 minutes. You could see two close together and then nothing at all for hours. We're all so used to being told exactly what to expect, but the night sky doesn't work like that — you need to be open to whatever it throws at you (or not). Once you stop expecting the sky to do what you want, meteor showers become more enjoyable.

Stargazer's corner: Oct. 31-Nov. 5, 2026

The moon is moving out of the early evening sky this week, which is exactly what stargazers wait for at this time of year. It reaches third quarter around Nov. 1, rising later at night and leaving the evening dark. That gives us a useful 10-night window for observing before moonlight becomes an issue.

I'm planning to use it for the Andromeda galaxy. From a genuinely dark location, M31 can be spotted with the naked eye as a faint patch. From brighter suburban skies, binoculars make life much easier. The beginner mistake is expecting anything resembling the photographs. Through binoculars, I'm looking for a subtle misty glow, not spiral arms. If you want a more impressive view, get yourself a smart telescope — they do a wonderful job on M31.

There's another practical change this weekend. Daylight saving time ends across most of the U.S. and Canada on Nov. 1. The stars haven't changed their schedule, of course, but getting outside under a dark sky after dinner — and even before — suddenly becomes much easier.

Constellation of the week: Taurus

Although you don't need to stare at Taurus, the Bull, to see Taurids, it's an obvious target this week. It's climbing into the eastern sky during the evening. Bright orange star Aldebaran — a red giant 67 light-years from the solar system (and the most luminous star within 100 light-years) — marks the bull's eye. It appears to sit within a V-shape of stars that forms the bull's face. This is the Hyades, the closest open cluster of stars to the solar system at just 150 light-years.

My latest stargazing obsession

The origin story of both Taurid meteor showers is genuinely awe-inspiring. They're associated with debris left in the inner solar system by Comet 2P/Encke, which orbits the sun once every 3.25 years (1,200 days) — the shortest orbital period of any known comet in the solar system, according to NASA. The second comet ever discovered, Encke, was discovered in 1786 and spans about 3 miles (4.8 kilometers) in diameter. It last reached perihelion — its closest point to the sun — on Oct. 22, 2023, and is due to do so again on Feb. 10, 2027, but Earth encounters debris associated with the comet every year.

The picture is more complicated than a single comet trail. The Southern and Northern Taurids are part of the broader Taurid Meteoroid Complex, a vast swarm of interplanetary dust, rocks, comets and asteroids thought to be related to Encke. It's thought that it originates from a much larger object that fragmented as it got close to the sun, perhaps just 5,000 to 6,000 years ago or as much as 20,000 years ago. Fears that huge, mile-wide "planet killer" asteroids may still reside in the Taurid Meteoroid Complex appear to have been ruled out. Phew.

Each fall, Earth passes through different parts of this sprawling stream, producing two overlapping meteor showers — and, occasionally, the larger fragments responsible for the Taurids' famous fireballs.

George Takei, who portrayed Lt. Hikaru Sulu and co-starred with Koenig on two seasons of "The Original Series" from 1967-69, as well as six subsequent "Star Trek" feature films, offered similar thoughts in memoriam.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 30, 1964: NASA's weird Lunar Landing Research Vehicle takes 1st test flight to help Apollo astronauts land on the moon ]]>

On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time.

The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11, the first crewed lunar landing.

The first person to give it a whirl was the X-15 pilot Joe Walker. During this test flight, he reached an altitude of about 10 feet, and he hovered there for about a minute. He did this two more times that same day. In all, he completed more than 30 test flights with the LLRV.

These test flights took place at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in Edwards, California. That facility has since been renamed the Armstrong Flight Research Center after Neil Armstrong, who also piloted — and famously crashed — the "Flying Bedstead" before he went to the moon.

Why it mattered

Over 60 years ago this LLRV test flight was a critical step toward landing humans on the moon for the first time, a historic moment that both served an important political purpose while also showcasing the result of monumental scientific and technical progress.

While images from this test flight might look like the team are having a bit of fun out in the desert, and perhaps they were, it was also deadly serious. The astronauts who signed onto these crewed missions were doing something that had never been attempted. They were putting their lives on the line for this progress, and this testing was a major piece in reassuring them and NASA that lunar landing could be accomplished, and safely.

Today, as we return humans to the moon with NASA's Artemis program, we see parallels between testing done over 60 years ago and testing today. Right now, SpaceX and Blue Origin are testing their lunar landers for crewed lunar landings in the near-future. While we have now been to the moon and have safely and successfully landed humans before, these tests remain critical for the safety and success of the missions.

]]> <![CDATA[ Ghostly Cat's Head Nebula haunts the cosmos | Space photo of the day for Oct. 30, 2026 ]]>

This "cat's head" would work perfectly in a witch's cauldron, glowing red "eyes" and all.

Just in time for Halloween, we have new, ghostly views of the Cat's Eye Nebula haunting the outer reaches of the cosmos.

What is it?

This nebula earned its name from its distinctive "cat's head" shape, which you can see on the left-hand side of these two images snapped by both the Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes. In these new images, you can even see the cat's glowing red "eye," which experts suggest could be a young star trapped in the nebula's dusty clutches.

Found about 7,500 light-years away from Earth, this star-forming region can be found within the larger Carina Nebula.

As the stars in the Carina Nebula continue to form, grow and evolve over time, the Nebula itself will change and eventually, this "cat's head" won't look much like a cat anymore. But for now, we can enjoy this vision of a domestic cat somehow depicted in this colossal tour of gas and dust.

Why is it incredible?

As a special Halloween treat, we have not one, but three new images of the cosmic cat's head.

In the snapshot captured by Hubble, we can see the nebula in visible light. This view shows the nebula as a brown pillar of dust embedded in a hazy, almost rainbow field of dust and gas. These colors are captured through Hubble's filters that can see the light coming from oxygen, hydrogen and sulfur and the light scattered by nebula dust.

JWST also took a look at this cat's head, observing the nebula in near- and mid-infrared wavelengths.

By looking at the same objects in space through different wavelengths and with different instruments and telescopes, we can uncover completely new and different details about these far-off celestial objects.

]]> <![CDATA[ Watch Virgin Galactic's new 'Delta-class' space plane take to the skies for the 1st time (video) ]]>

Virgin Galactic's first "Delta-class" space plane just made its maiden voyage.

The next-gen suborbital vehicle, named Apeiron (Greek for "Boundless"), lifted off for the first time ever on Thursday (Oct. 28). Flying beneath the wings of its carrier aircraft, VMS Eve, Apeiron traveled from Virgin's manufacturing site in Mesa, Arizona, to its launch site, Spaceport America in New Mexico.

"Seeing the ship fly beneath Eve to Spaceport America was a moment years in the making," Virgin Galactic CEO Michael Colglazier said in a statement on Thursday. "To our team and our astronaut community: your Spaceship has arrived."

Apeiron will undergo a series of checks and tests at Spaceport America, leading up to a planned start of commercial service in the spring of 2027.

During those customer flights, Eve will carry Apeiron to an altitude of about 45,000 feet (13,700 meters), then drop the space plane. Apeiron will fire up its onboard rocket motor, which will carry the six-passenger, two-pilot vehicle to suborbital space.

Passengers will experience a few minutes of weightlessness and get to see the curve of Earth against the blackness of space before coming down for a runway landing back at Spaceport America.

Virgin Galactic has done this before, with its VSS Unity space plane. Unity flew seven commercial suborbital missions during its operational life, which ran from June 2023 to June 2024.

Apeiron and other Delta-class planes are built for a much heavier workload, according to Virgin Galactic.

"Designed to fly twice per week with a vehicle lifetime of more than 500 missions, each Spaceship in the next-generation fleet is built to support the economics of a scaled commercial operation, with increased flight cadence and a cost profile unprecedented in the industry," company representatives wrote in the same statement.

And there will indeed be a fleet, if all goes to plan. The second Delta ship is under construction, for example, and is expected to enter service in mid-2027, according to Virgin Galactic.

"We measured how the planet's brightness and heat changed throughout its orbit," team member Lisa Dang of the University of Waterloo said in a statement. "This technique, known as a phase curve, revealed that the planet reflects a significant amount of light from its star, and that heat is being redistributed around the planet instead of only on the sunlit side. Together, these point to the presence of an atmosphere."

The hemispheres of lava super-Earth are day and night

The proximity of TOI-561 b to its star has another consequence. The planet is tidally locked, meaning it doesn't turn like Earth. Thus, TOI-561 b has one blisteringly hot "dayside" permanently facing its star, and a cooler "nightside" facing out into space in perpetuity.

Dang and colleagues investigated the fact that the bare rock of the dayside seemed to be cooler than should be expected. They theorized that missing heat could be carried around to the night side or the heat may be reflected away before TOI-561 b can absorb it.

By using the JWST to observe full orbits of TOI-561 b, the team was able to observe the planet's nightside for the first time. They found it isn't warm enough to account for all the heat missing from the dayside.

The team determined that this high reflectivity is the result of clouds of silicate minerals, including silicon dioxide and magnesium silicate, forming on the planet's dayside and acting like sunscreen. These clouds could also help TOI-561 b hang on to an atmosphere.

Of course, the team can't yet be sure what this atmosphere is composed of. It could be a dense carbon dioxide fog like that seen on Venus, or it could be a blanket of sulfur dioxide like that of the most volcanic body in the solar system, Jupiter's moon Io. That would be the case if, like on Io, volcanic activity is replenishing the atmosphere of TOI-561 b.

"The next big question we will seek to answer is whether TOI-561 b's atmosphere resembles Venus or an extreme version of Io," Dang said. On Oct. 29, 1991, the Galileo spacecraft flew by the asteroid Gaspra on its way to Jupiter. Gaspra was the first asteroid to ever be visited by a spacecraft.

Gaspra orbits near the inner edge of the asteroid belt. The Galileo spacecraft had been travelling through the asteroid belt for about two months before it reached Gaspra. Galileo was 990 miles (1,593 kilometers) away from Gaspra when it whizzed by, and it was travelling at a relative speed of about 5 miles (8 km) per second.

The spacecraft took several photos of the asteroid and used an instrument called the Near-Infrared Mapping Spectrometer to study its chemical composition and other physical properties. Galileo determined that Gaspra has an irregular and elongated shape measuring about 12 miles long and 7 miles wide. The images revealed that Gaspra was also covered in craters. Because Galileo was too far away for Gaspra's gravity to affect it, the spacecraft was not able to determine the asteroid's mass.

Why it mattered

The Galileo spacecraft's flyby of Gaspra was a pitstop near the midpoint of its 6-year journey to Jupiter, the largest planet in our solar system. NASA launched Galileo toward Jupiter in October 1989, with the probe swinging by Venus and Earth in 1990 before its encounter with Gaspra.

The Gaspra flyby was the first asteroid flyby in history, with Galileo approaching to just under 1,000 miles (1,601 kilometers) while flying at a whopping 18,000 mph. Galileo's photos of Gaspra "revealed a cratered, complex, irregular body about 20 by 12 by 11 kilometers (12.4 by 7.4 by 6.8 miles), with a thin covering of dust and rubble," NASA wrote in an overview.

"The picture we get of Gaspra is one of something that has suffered a lot during its history," the UPI press service quoted Joseph Veverka, a Galileo imaging team member, as saying at the time. "We suspect that this is the survivor of a series of catastrophic collisions in the past."

Galileo would go on to fly by Earth a second time in 1992, then swing close by the asteroid Ida in 1993 before finally arriving at Jupiter in 1995. Along the way, the probe was in the right place at the right time to watch as the Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 broke into pieces and crashed into Jupiter in July 1994.

Since Galileo's historic first asteroid flyby, NASA and other space agencies have gone on to land on asteroids (like NEAR on asteroid Eros), collect samples of asteroids and return them to Earth (like NASA's OSIRIS-REx and Japan's Hayabusa probes), and have even intentionally crashed probes into asteroids (like NASA's DART asteroid impact mission) to test planetary protection techniques.

   <description>Nizozemská společnost Ahold, která v ČR provozuje prodejny Albert, kupuje Tesco v ČR a na Slovensku. I s nájemními závazky zaplatí zhruba 1,7 miliardy eur (v přepočtu kolem 41,4 miliardy Kč). Dokončení transakce po splnění obvyklých podmínek, včetně schválení regulačními orgány, firma očekává ve čtvrtém čtvrtletí příštího roku. V tiskové zprávě o tom v pátek informoval mluvčí řetězce Albert Jiří Mareček. Tesco tak skončí na českém trhu po 30 letech. Akvizice zahrnuje i prodejny Žabka, které provozuje Tesco Franchise ČR, řekla ČTK za společnost Tesco Charlotte Haney.</description>

výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:47:35 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.4 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Mandava Jazz / Mandau Jazz 2026 – Iva Bittová & Duo Jedlinský–Fischer https://www.vybezek.eu/296291-mandava-jazz-mandau-jazz-2026-iva-bittova-duo-jedlinsky-fischer/ Thu, 29 Oct 2026 18:16:24 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296291 Další večer u Kocoura – Mezinárodní hudební festival Mandava Jazz 2026 tentokrát ve středu 28. září 2026, opět ve varnsdorfském pivovaru Kocour, dorazila Iva Bittová a duo Jedlinský & Fischer.

Stejně jako nedávného Dana Bártu i Ivu Bittovou jsme už zažili několikrát (2011 na Vlčí hoře nebo 2017 v divadle). Vždy jako personu velmi osobitou, která si s nástrojem, hlasem a jazykem (nebo spíš jazyky, chvílemi to vypadalo na hudební esperanto-svahilštinu), dělá co chce. A vždy bravurně. Ačkoli ona sama je většinou tahákem na plakátech a v upoutávkách, sama sebe neupřednostňuje a dává spoustu prostoru všem, se kterými v tu kterou chvíli spolupracuje.

Iva Bittová – zpěv, housle; Jakub Jedlinský – akordeon, zpěv; Pavel Fischer – housle, zpěv

Inu, někdo je Fotograf a umí (snad) zachytit neuchopitelnou atmosféru, vyjádřit obrazem zážitek z hudby. Já mezi takové nepatřím, nejsem fotograf. Jsem jen přítomen.

]]> Šluknovská liga 2026/2027 – futsal https://www.vybezek.eu/296177-sluknovska-liga-2026-2027-futsal/ Wed, 21 Oct 2026 22:03:22 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296177 Ve středu 21. října 2026 se konalo první sportovní klání Šluknovské ligy, žáci některých výběžkových škol se utkali v Dolní Poustevně ve futsale.
Pravidelná a tradiční sportovní soutěž škol Šluknovského výběžku (dle loňských textů letos 34. ročník). A jako vždy dílčí informace od některých účastnících se škol:

Základní škola Jiříkov:

Ve středu 21. 10. 2026 byl futsalovým turnajem zahájen další ročník Šluknovské ligy. V Dolní Poustevně jsme byli první !!!. Až později dorazil do haly domácí tým a po něm zbývající 4 družstva. Tím náš velký úspěch skončil. Naši hráči se snažili trefit správné zařízení, kterému se říká branka soupeře, a nakonec se nám tato činnost dolní končetiny povedla 4x a pokaždé jinému střelci. Šancí bylo více, ale na ty se nehraje. Trochu jsme zamotali tabulkou svým jediným vítězstvím nad třetím Šluknovem, ale nakonec jsme se umístili na 6. místě. Nutno podotknout, že polovinu našeho repre týmu tvořili nováčci ze 6. třídy, pro které byla velká zkušenost hrát proti o dva až tři roky starším chlapcům. Nejdůležitější je, že si všichni zahráli, naši kluci zůstali zdraví, nikdo nebyl CHORÝ a chovali se v rámci fair-play. Za měsíc jdou do boje děvčata v přehazované, tak jim držme palce, aby naše umístění vylepšila.

J. Kolář

Základní škola a Mateřská škola Dolní Poustevna:

Šluknovská liga – futsal. ZŠ Dolní Poustevna – krásné 4. místo. Gratulujeme!

Základní škola J. Vohradského Šluknov:

První sportovní soutěží Šluknovské ligy v ročníku 2026/2027 byl, jako již tradičně, futsal.

Náš tým tvořili žáci napříč celým druhým stupněm: Kristián D., Antonín V., Matyáš H., Matyáš H., Josef B., Jakub V., G. C., David V. a Petr S.

Všem hráčům děkujeme za jejich nasazení, sportovní přístup a reprezentaci školy.

V celkovém pořadí jsme obsadili krásné 3. místo. Gratulujeme k dosaženému výsledku!

]]> Turnaj Jr. NBA League, 1. hrací kolo divize E – 21. 10. 2026 Šluknov https://www.vybezek.eu/296193-turnaj-jr-nba-league-1-hraci-kolo-divize-e-21-10-2026-sluknov/ Wed, 21 Oct 2026 21:49:30 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296193 Po jarní kvalifikační části (a po divizi F ve VDF) se ve středu 21. října 2026 konal turnaj dalšího ročníku Jr. NBA League ve Šluknově.

Web Schrödingerova institutu:

Ve středu 21. října se ve Šluknově odehrálo hrací kolo Západní ligy Jr. NBA, divize E, které organizačně zajistila Basketbalová akademie Šluknovska při Schrödingerově institutu.

Na palubovce se představilo pět školních týmů, které bojovaly nejen o vítězství, ale především o dvě postupová místa do další fáze soutěže.

Konečné pořadí divize E:
1. ZŠ Mozartova, Jablonec nad Nisou
2. ZŠ Vojtěcha Kováře, Rumburk
3. ZŠ Tyršova, Rumburk
4. ZŠ J. Vohradského, Šluknov
5. ZŠ Jiříkov

O druhém postupujícím rozhodoval doslova jediný bod! Obě rumburské školy odehrály vzájemný zápas s nerozhodným výsledkem 6:6 a o konečném pořadí tak rozhodoval rozdíl ve skóre ze všech utkání. Ten měla ZŠ Vojtěcha Kováře lepší o pouhý jeden bod, a zajistila si tak postup společně s vítěznou školou z Jablonce nad Nisou. Šluknovská základní škola obsadila se svým jedním vítězstvím čtvrté místo, pátý Jiříkov tentokrát na výhru nedosáhl.

Gratulujeme oběma postupujícím týmům a všem ostatním děkujeme za skvělé sportovní nasazení, bojovnost a fair play! Velké poděkování patří také všem, kteří se podíleli na organizaci turnaje, trenérům, pedagogům i rozhodčím.

Jsme rádi, že Basketbalová akademie Šluknovska může být součástí projektu Jr. NBA a přinášet dětem z našeho regionu další příležitosti zažít atmosféru opravdové basketbalové soutěže.
Basketbal nás spojuje!

Oficiální web akce je na tom stále stejně (viz minulý text), nic nic nic a ještě jednou nic. A tentokrát na tom o moc lépe nejsou ani zúčastněné školy.

Základní škola Jiříkov na FB:

Žáci ZŠ Jiříkov bojovali v juniorské NBA lize

Dne 21. 10. 2026 se žáci 2. až 5. tříd ZŠ Jiříkov zúčastnili juniorské NBA ligy, kde bojovali o postup do dalšího kola.

Přestože se jim tentokrát nepodařilo zvítězit a postoupit do užšího výběru, zaslouží si velkou pochvalu. Do hry dali všechny své síly, bojovali statečně a nevzdávali se. Ukázali své přednosti a zároveň poznali, v čem se mohou dál zlepšovat.

Zápasy jim přinesly cenné zkušenosti i motivaci do dalších tréninků. Děkujeme všem našim hráčům a hráčkám za reprezentaci školy, nasazení a odhodlání!
